text:
maria: Quick heads up — our int8 + split-packing run on the shared inference pool showed a small but sharp hallucination/formatting spike on the table->json benchmark. attaching quick notes.
kevin: Which model & quant path? AWQ on gptx-small? any fp8 runs for comparison?
maria: AWQ-INT8 on rw/gptx-7b-like (v2). baseline FP16 run: hallucination ~0.8% across eval set. int8+splitpack: hallucination ~4.5%. JSON formatting errors up from 0.3% -> ~3.1% (missing/truncated braces)
ci-bot: [run/2109876500] nightly-eval: int8-splitpack-multi-tenant — flaky json format failures flagged (see /runs/2109876500/log)
tara: That pattern screams sequence-boundary KV bleed. split-packing can merge tails/heads across different requests if tenant isolation isn't enforced.
devon: We hit something similar last quarter when pack_size>1 on shared pools and kv_cache was global. Pack merges + no eos trimming -> token overlap -> structured output corruption.
maria: Quick config snippet from the failing job:
```
model: rw/gptx-7b-like:v2-awq-int8
packing:
  enabled: true
  pack_size: 2
kv_cache:
  mode: shared
tenant_isolation: false
```
kevin: Try pack_size=1 and tenant_isolation=true as a control. Also try pack_size=2 but per-tenant cache.
eva: Proposed repro matrix:
- pack_size: 1,2,4
- kv_cache: shared, per-tenant
- quant: awq-int8, gptq-int8, fp16
Run each on the same seeded eval subset (1000 examples) and measure: hallucination rate, json parse failures, token-level insertions around boundaries.
maria: I already ran a quick sweep:
pack_size=1 + shared -> halluc 0.9% json_fail 0.4%
pack_size=2 + shared -> halluc 4.5% json_fail 3.1%
pack_size=4 + shared -> halluc 6.8% json_fail 5.2%
pack_size=2 + per-tenant -> halluc 1.1% json_fail 0.5% (so isolation helps)
tara: Nice — that strongly implicates cross-request KV contamination. We should also check eos/pad handling: if the runtime drops eos tokens during packing, next request can pick up "open" JSON tokens.
devon: Also note quantization noise: AWQ-int8 may make the model more brittle to small token shifts, so the same boundary bleed produces larger semantic errors vs fp16.
kevin: Actionable next steps:
- run focused bisect varying only pack_size with logging of token streams around request boundaries (capture last 32 tokens of request and first 32 of next)
- instrument runtime to annotate when pack fused requests cross tenant ids
- add a quick canary to route a sample tenant to an isolated pool (tenant_isolation=true)
- test gptq-int8 for comparison
maria: I'm going to spin a canary: AWQ-int8, pack_size=1 on a tenant-isolated pool and rerun the full table->json eval. ETA ~2h.
eva: I'll queue the bisect matrix on the evaluation cluster. adding scripts to dump the raw token sequences to /tmp/seq-dumps-210987.
ci-bot: job queued: eval-matrix-210987 (6 jobs). estimated finish ~3h.
kevin: Also create a regression alert tied to JSON parse failures on table->json route (if >1% over baseline trigger).
tara: Good call. If pack-level speedups are causing correctness regressions on structured-output tasks we should default pack_size to 1 for routes flagged as "structured-output" unless explicit tenant-isolation is on.
maria: Assigning owners: @kevin (bisect + alert), @tara (runtime instrumentation + suggestion to default pack_size for structured routes). I'll attach the failing logs & sample token dumps to a ticket.
kevin: I'll take it. thanks. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks everyone. Will post updates once the canary finishes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
